messages.author: 03290ff051991093
messages.subject: Cleaning Up temp Files
parts:
All,

The tutorial mentions at several points that big data objects clean up after themselves when the data is no longer needed. For example, "to.dfs can put the data in a file of your own choosing, but if you don't specify one it will create temp files and clean them up when done."

However, when I run the following simple example, I see that some temp files are created in hdfs://localhost:9000/tmp, but the are not cleaned up (even when I close R later):
small.ints = to.dfs(1:1000)
rm(small.ints)

Thanks,
M

Thanks a lot for the fix.

Now I have two follow-up questions.

1) Is it possible to somehow change the settings such that a different directory is used by rmr2 for the temp files instead of the /tmp directory? I'm asking since I have set up two users, one for Hadoop admin ("hdadmin"), the other one ("hduser") for using Hadoop (e.g. with rmr2). Currently I have set dfs.permissions to false in conf/hdfs-site.xml, otherwise hduser has sometimes problems  writing to /tmp. So I think it would be better if I could, for example, have rmr2 use /user/hduser/tmp for temporary files instead of /tmp. This way I would not have to disable the enforcement of HDFS file permissions.

2) Now rmr2 seems to clean up the files in the temp directory it has created (/tmp/RtmpmRxrvP in the example above). However, when all variables in this directory are gone and thus all temp files have been created, the temp directory /tmp/RtmpmRxrvP still persists. I am aware that this might be so because if some new big data object is created, you don't need to create another temp directory. On the other hand, over time, this might clutter the /tmp directory. Of course, it possible to simply manually delete everything in /tmp every now and then, but I am wondering whether it is possible to also clean up the /tmp/RtmpmRxrvP folder.

Anyway, thanks for your excellent work with RHadoop.

Best,
M
